The Refounder re-wraps those heads at the new epoch's Control address, under the new community_root-derived read key, signed by the freshly minted control_root's signer: a re-wrap, never a re-signing, so the original authors' signatures survive into an epoch they were not written in (the reason CORD-02 §5 makes these seals plaintext). Ordered per CORD-06 §3 — the re-anchor runs only after every rekey chunk's publication is confirmed and this device has adopted; a failure there is not a failed Refounding (the roll landed, republishing heads is idempotent, the Refounder resumes). Abort rule enforced before the first publish: a plane with parked editions (count_parked > 0) is one whose fold is unsettled, so refound_async refuses rather than compacting past an action nobody can yet judge. Tests: /concord/refound/re-anchors-control (a joiner holding only its rekey blob's new root + control_pk and not one prior edition folds the rename and a Grant-derived permission from the compaction alone; 5 editions in, 4 heads out — the superseded metadata version is what it never replays) and /concord/refound/aborts-on-unsettled-control (parked edition blocks the rotation with nothing published, and the same rotation proceeds once the cited Grant lands). All 4 refound tests plus the full concord suite green under ASan. Commit 0e79b5d7.

Publishing half landed as the Refounding's final, best-effort step. After the root roll and the Control re-anchor, the Rotator publishes the prior epoch's present members — the same Complete Memberlist the blobs were addressed to — as kind-3312 rumors in encrypted seals at the NEW epoch's Guestbook address, chunked at CONCORD_SNAPSHOT_CHUNK_SIZE (400) with ['snap', id, i, n]. The snapshot id is the rotation's prevcommit, so a resumed Refounder re-publishes the same set rather than racing a second one. Failures emit an error and leave the Refounding successful (a member finding their own state absent republishes a Join, so an unsent snapshot is a blip where a failed rotation would be a fork). Receiving half was already complete (nostrc-3mkc); what closes the loop is that adopt_base_rotation() sets the refounder from the rotation the device just adopted, so a receiver learns whom to honor from the rotation itself and not from the snapshot claiming it. Test /concord/refound/seeds-guestbook: a device that adopts the rotation with no Guestbook fold of its own is offered every published event, opens exactly the one chunk at its new Guestbook address, and ends up with all three prior-epoch members — proving both the seeding and the refounder attribution. Full concord suite green under ASan. Commit a80eda37.

The debt is now recorded from the fold, not only from this client's own retire. apply_control_fold() tracks the Public/Private state it last folded (public_known/was_public on CommunityState) and records refounding_due_epoch = root_epoch + 1 when the aggregate active-set is seen *becoming* empty, whoever published the Registry edition that emptied it. Deliberately a transition and never a reading of current state: a Registry edition carries no epoch, so an empty set alone cannot distinguish a fresh retire from one a Refounding paid years ago — a device that arrives to an empty set has observed no transition and owes nothing. What made this sound is nostrc-hlyn's compaction: after a Refounding the history containing the old transition is no longer republished at the new epoch's address, so the only transitions left to observe are ones that genuinely owe. The local-retire path stays (it fires before the edition echoes back) and both are idempotent, guarded by refounding_due_epoch <= root_epoch. The debt still pays itself by the root roll. Tests: /concord/refound/debt-from-another-staffer (arriving Private owes nothing; mint then a retire published by the owner alone raises the debt on a device that only ever saw the editions) and /concord/refound/pays-the-debt (the rotation clears it with nothing resetting a flag). Full concord suite green under ASan. Commit f4d734a0.

Independent single-Channel rotation landed; the two clauses that were bundled here are split out with precise notes (nostrc-ay29 Refounding integration, nostrc-r874 race convergence). The rotation path is now scoped rather than base-only: one implementation carries a scope that decides the address, the blob width, the epoch that moves and the permission it takes. Base = 104/136 bytes at the all-zero scope, BAN, moves the root; Channel = 72 bytes at the Channel id, MANAGE_CHANNELS, moves only that Channel's key. Shared: locator search, continuity check over the key held now, chunking at 120, and the rule that only a complete set without this npub's locator is a removal. New surface: gn_concord_community_service_rekey_channel_async/_finish (excluded-member list, refuses a public Channel outright and refuses to exclude anyone the Rotator does not strictly outrank — enforced at the mint so an unenforceable rotation never reaches the wire), gn_concord_community_service_ingest_channel_rekey_wrap(), a per-Private-Channel rekey subscription at the precomputed next address, adopt_channel_rotation(), and gn_concord_channel_item_set_key(key, epoch) which moves key and epoch together because the plane address derives from both. Addressed under the community_root rather than the Channel key it replaces (CORD-06 §2), which is what keeps a member losing the Channel reachable and what ay29 depends on. Found and fixed a real hole while testing: the shared locator derived at the base scope unconditionally, so a Channel rotation would have addressed every blob to a locator nobody computes — a rotation delivering nothing, which every recipient reads as everyone being removed. Tests /concord/rekey/channel-roundtrip (rotate, adopt, converge on a message in the rotated Channel, a stale device cannot find the address, and the base epoch is untouched so no Refounding is owed) and /concord/rekey/channel-refusals (public Channel, and a Rotator without MANAGE_CHANNELS). All 45 concord tests green under ASan. Commit 17257877.

Refounding now rotates every held Private Channel between the last base rekey chunk and adopt_base_rotation(), so each rotation is sealed and addressed under the prior community_root and stays openable on either branch of a racing base rotation. Conservative set (every Private Channel this device holds a key for), captured before the first publish alongside the Memberlist and Control heads. A Refounder holding BAN but not MANAGE_CHANNELS is refused up front when it holds Private Channel keys, since every recipient enforces MANAGE_CHANNELS on a channel-scoped rotation and a half-severing would look complete. Per-Channel failures mid-flight are reported and non-fatal — the base roll is already published by then. Test /concord/refound/rotates-private-channels drives two racing Refoundings and shows a member on either branch opens a message in the rotated Channel.
